hints: It is a wheeled seat for moving a person.
Look near the middle of the room, close to the right wall.
questions.explanation: The patient transport chair has a seat, backrest, armrests, footrests and wheels, and is used to move a seated patient between areas.

hints: It is a tall unit on a pedestal.
It stands against the right-hand wall.
questions.explanation: The CT injection system is a pedestal-mounted unit used alongside CT scanners. In this module it is a visual teaching model only.

hints: It is a small brown cardboard box.
It is sitting on a table.
questions.explanation: Supply boxes like this are carried to a work surface and returned to storage afterwards.

hints: It is the largest object in the room.
It is shelving along the back wall.
questions.explanation: Storage racks keep boxed supplies off the floor and organised.

hints: It has a screen showing numbers.
It is mounted near the patient bed.
questions.explanation: A vital-sign monitor displays measurements such as heart rate and oxygen saturation. Values in this training are synthetic.

hints: It is where hands are washed with soap and water.
It is near the front wall, on the entrance side of the room.
questions.explanation: Hand hygiene stations are placed where staff can clean their hands on entering and leaving a care area.

hints: It is a container for used items.
It is in the front right corner.
questions.explanation: Waste containers are placed within reach of where used items are produced.

hints: It is a wheeled unit with a flat top.
It is in the middle of the room's front half.
questions.explanation: A supply cart brings commonly used items to the point of care.

hints: It is the bed with side rails.
It is on the left side of the room.
questions.explanation: The patient bed is the central piece of furniture in a patient care room.

hints: It is a closed unit that locks.
It stands against the left wall.
questions.explanation: Closed cabinets hold supplies that should be kept clean and out of sight.
